fatalFlaws: Control-rate destinations STEP once per 32 samples with no intra-tick ramp: inside `if samplesToTick == 0:` the design does `loop.setDecay (clamp (decayKnob + dm.decay, 0, 1.15))`, `blend = clamp (blendKnob + dm.blend, 0, 1) -> equal-power gains`, `strengthGain = dbToGain (...)`. The 3 ms `ctrlSlew` only limits each step to ~20% of the remaining move, so the hero Follower->Decay route (5 ms attack, +0.14 feedback) puts a ~0.03 gain step train at 1.5 kHz onto a near-saturated feedback signal at every note onset, and a modulated Blend/Strength puts it on the output. Knob smoothers are also only read per tick ("combined ... once per tick"), which downgrades the template's per-sample gain path. Zipper, not a click, but it is on the hero route and must not ship.

Agitate / Time Mod macros are unsmoothed: `void setMacros (float agitate01, float timeMod01); // per block` and `timeAgitGain = macroTime * modk::timeRangeOct * depth[agitation][time]` is applied directly per sample in `timeOctForSample`. A host automating Time Mod steps the audio-rate FM depth per block (up to +-2 oct * (2a-1) in one sample). Violates CLAUDE.md's "all continuous parameters go through SmoothedValue".

Drift bound arithmetic is wrong by 2x: "3-sigma about 4.8 cents, bounded by tanh at 4.8 cents". Pitch of a variable-clock delay is 2^(L_read - L_write), so the rail-to-rail bound is 2 * 1200 * 0.004 = 9.6 cents, above the scenario's own `DRIFT_CENTS_MAX = 8`. The `drift` test can go red on a legitimate rail swing.
scores.notes: Strong on musical thinking and on test breadth: the `heat` long-memory term (rho +8 over 6 s) is the only thing in either design that gives Interference evolution on the 5-10 s scale; the relative-onset gate detector (env > 1.8x a 300 ms baseline, 60 ms refractory) retriggers on re-picks while a note rings, which Design 1's hysteresis cannot; the telescoping-pitch observation (fs(now)/fs(write) across k passes collapses to fs(now)/fs(original), so drift never random-walks) is correct and is why its Decay-1.05 drift test is meaningful. The `timefm` alias line (700 Hz Agitation point-sampled at 1.5 kHz aliasing to 800 Hz, must be < -40 dB) is the single best discriminator in either design for 'Time is really audio rate', and `agitateOnTime` surfaces a real UX question the plan leaves implicit. Weaknesses on my lens: forward Euler at `dtMax = 0.02` with rho pushed to 38 by heat is borderline (bounded in practice but inaccurate, and the `isfinite -> reset(seed)` escape produces a 4 ms slewed jump of up to +-1 oct into Time if it ever fires); Interference derives its output from `x` and needs a 0.3 Hz DC blocker to hide the fixed-point offset, where Design 1's `y - x` is zero at fixed points for free; no block-size invariance test at all (only 'same PASS lines at 44.1k/64 and 96k/512'); `timefm` does not specify Time, and the sideband amplitude depends on 700*tau mod 1 (at integer values the sidebands vanish); the `drift` scenario measures pitch by zero crossings on a saturated, hissy runaway loop, which is fragile at the 0.3 cent level it asserts. Agitation centred (`2a-1`) only on the Time column is defensible but makes one source behave differently per column. Everything derives from seconds; nothing allocates on the audio thread; state discipline is correctly stated as 'nothing to stamp in v1'. Bypass behaviour and EngineTest `ScopedNoDenormals` are explicitly covered, which Design 1 omits.

Wins on exactly the things my lens cares about. `ControlRamp` reads Decay/Absorb/Blend/Strength per sample across the 32-sample tick so gains never step; the persistent `samplesUntilTick` plus a test that demands bit-match to 1e-6 at block sizes 1/33/128/2048 is the right way to prove tick alignment; RK2 at dt <= 0.013 with hard state clamps at +-60 and a finite check makes the worst Lorenz outcome a stuck orbit; `y - x` as the wander output is zero at every fixed point so a calm loop gives exactly zero Time offset with no DC blocker; energy normalised in dB (-54..-6) rather than linearly (Design 0's `loopEnergy/0.25` leaves a -30 dBFS loop almost inert); the 3.6 bounded-map argument is explicit and the feedback bandwidth (3 ms/150 ms -> 20 ms/400 ms -> 40 Hz) is stated so breathing has a predicted period the test then measures; `kAgitMinSegmentMs = 0.5` prevents a 1% segment at 1 kHz becoming a one-sample ratio cliff; macro and Time Mod are smoothed (30 ms); `demodPitch` is the right pitch measurement on a lo-fi wet path and the square-wave follower test makes the 5 ms attack exact. It actually read JUCE (`reset(int)` snap, `Multiplicative`). Non-fatal but real defects: (1) `return sum / n // block mean` in `Agitation::process` is per SUB-block, so when a control block straddles a host block the ctl value is the mean of a partial block, which is block-size dependent and would fail its own 6.7 to-1e-6 claim; (2) skeleton says `matrix.tick(srcs, knobs.skip(kControlBlock))` while 3.4 says knobs are `skip(n)`'d per sub-block, pick one (skip(n)); (3) gate re-arm is `if followerEnv[i] < kGateOffLevel: armed = true`, so a sustaining guitar cannot retrigger until it decays under -36 dBFS, musically the weakest gate of the two; (4) the `generative` scenario runs Agitate 0.7 at 0.2 Hz (a 5 s periodic filter sweep) and simultaneously asserts 'RMS-envelope autocorrelation lags 2..40 s max < 0.6', which the 5 s cycle will likely violate by construction, and 'at least 3 windows where loop energy differs by 0.15' then merely measures the Agitation cycle; (5) `kLogFsHardMin = log2(1000)` lets modulation push the clock a third below the plan's 1.5 kHz floor (5.5 s, 450 Hz reconstruction LPF), harmless only if the PT core is explicitly voiced there, which the design does not require; (6) Speed readout '0.02 Hz' is against the CLAUDE.md readout rule, acknowledged only as risk 11; (7) no mention of `ScopedNoDenormals` in EngineTest loops even though `crackleTarget *= crackleDecay` and `crackleEnv` decay into denormals; (8) no bypass behaviour statement. Crackle at up to 400/s and +-0.6 oct in 0.3 ms is a taste risk (can read as broken tape rather than static) but every knob of it is a constant and the pulses are C0-continuous in the ratio, so no click.

graft: Persistent Agitation accumulator across sub-blocks (Design 0's `agitSum += a` per sample, `agitSum * invInterval` at the tick, then reset): replaces Design 1's per-sub-block `sum / n` and is what makes the block-size-invariance test actually pass.

Relative-onset gate detector from Design 0 (env > `folk::gateOnLin` = -30 dBFS AND env > 1.8x a 300 ms lagging baseline, 60 ms refractory, baseline updated AFTER the test), evaluated per sample inside Design 1's `Agitation::process` so trigger latency stays zero. Keep Design 1's soft retrigger from `lastOut * faEff`.

Design 0's `heat` term: `heat += heatCoeff * (s - heat)` with `intk::heatSeconds = 6`, `rho += intk::heatRho * heat` (8), so a loop that has been hot for a while gets wilder; it is the only long-timescale evolution mechanism in either design. Cap rho at Design 1's 45 and keep RK2.

Speed readout per Design 0 and the infinite_sustainer Sweep Rate precedent: below 1 Hz show the period ('62.5 s', one decimal), 1..100 Hz two decimals, >= 100 Hz integers, unit baked into the string, parameter label empty. Range via the `logRange` helper (genuine exponential), never `setSkewForCentre`.

Split the generative gate as Design 0 does: `generative` with Agitate 0 (only Interference->Time, the drift trim and in-loop noise move anything) carries the non-repeat / pattern-ACF assertions; `generative-agitated` (Agitate 0.6, Speed 0.05 Hz) drops the ACF line and adds centroid std >= 150 Hz. Keep Design 1's breathing-period assertion on `e` (autocorr peak 0.5..5 s) on both.

Design 0's chaos triad of tests: 'chaotic not merely noisy' (second run same seed with one extra 1e-5 input sample, NRMSD over 80..90 s > 0.5), 'deterministic when seeded' (FNV over 30..90 s equal), 'production runs differ' (two engines without `seedForTests`, FNV differ), plus the class-level Interference sensitive-dependence check (1e-6 perturbation: RMS diff < 1e-3 over 0..0.5 s, > 0.3 over 5..10 s).

Design 0's `timefm` alias-line assertion: with Agitation at 700 Hz into Time, the control-rate alias at 1500 - 700 = 800 Hz must be < -40 dB re carrier while the 300/1700 Hz sidebands are present. Specify Time explicitly (Design 1's Time 0.2 so 700*tau mod 1 is not near 0), and keep Design 1's 'route back on Filter only -> sidebands within 3 dB of Time Mod 0' control.

Design 0's drift-under-runaway scenario (220 Hz burst, Decay 1.05, Time Mod 0, drift trim only, 2..40 s), because it is the only test of the telescoping property (pitch = fs(now)/fs(original write), no random walk across passes). Measure it with Design 1's `demodPitch`, not zero crossings, and set the bound to 2 * 1200 * kDriftTimeOct (rail-to-rail), not 1x. Keep Design 1's Decay-0 `drifttime` as the single-pass version and its `setDriftDepthForTests(0)` floor check.

`juce::ScopedNoDenormals` in every EngineTest scenario loop (Design 0's harness note): the Lorenz ring-down, the follower tail, the DC/HP blockers and Design 1's crackle decays all produce denormals and offline runs would otherwise be slow and numerically different from the plugin.

Design 0's bypass statement: the engine keeps running while bypassed and sees silence (follower falls, Interference rings down, Agitation keeps its phase); Clear flushes buffers and filter states only, never Agitation phase or Lorenz/drift state.

Design 0's `modk::agitateOnTime` (Design 1: `kMacroScalesAllRoutes`) as an explicit compile-time switch for whether Agitate multiplies the Time column; ship whichever the user picks, but keep the constant so the A/B is one line.

Design 0's `fastExp2` (6th-order polynomial on the fraction, exponent bits via memcpy, ~1.5e-5 relative) as the profiled fallback for the per-sample `exp2f`, and Design 0's 'never go per-block, `timefm` would fail' note in the code comment.

Design 0's separate always-on drift trim summed OUTSIDE the matrix and OUTSIDE the +-2 oct clamp (Design 1 already does this; keep it) with Design 0's smaller `driftk::timeDepthOct = 0.004` as the starting value, since Design 1's 0.006 gives ~14 cents rail-to-rail at long Time which is vibrato, not clock wander.
unresolved: Whether Agitate scales the Time column (plan-literal: 'the Agitate macro scales all three', Design 1) or Time Mod is independent so it is never a dead knob at Agitate 0 (Design 0's default). Both designs punt to a constant; it is the user's call and it changes the Init preset.

Tell 5 (audio-rate ring-mod sidebands) is unreachable from the v1 UI in BOTH designs: Agitation->Time ships at depth 0 and the hardware's normalled sub-osc source is Phase 4. Either ship a nonzero hidden Agitation->Time depth, or accept that the tell is test-only until Tones exists.

Gate mode on sustained/legato sources: Design 0's relative-onset detector needs +5 dB over the ring-out, Design 1's hysteresis needs a fall below -36 dBFS. Neither is the HF-band transient detector infinite_sustainer uses; a real guitar test will decide whether that upgrade is needed in Phase 3 or can wait.

Interference character (crackle density/amplitude vs wander, energy floor vs the PT core's idle hiss at longest Time, ring-down length after the loop dies). Both designs correctly say this needs an ear and a tuning pass; neither can specify a number that the tests would meaningfully assert beyond 'correlates with loop energy'.

Self-start of the generative milestone depends on the Phase 1/2 in-loop noise and quantisation levels, not on the modulation system. Neither design quantifies the noise floor required for `SELFSTART_MAX_S` or for Design 1's `kEnergyFloorDb = -54` to sit 6 dB above idle hiss; that coupling has to be measured once the core is voiced.

How the PT core's read side behaves when `ratio` changes by up to +-0.6 oct within 14 samples (Design 1 crackle) or by a one-sample step (Design 0 with angle exposed): both designs assert 'the accumulator is shared so it is continuous' but neither specifies or tests the core's interpolation under a fast ratio slope, which is where a click would actually come from if one exists.

Whether modulation may push fs_chip below the plan's 1.5 kHz floor (Design 1's `kLogFsHardMin = log2(1000)`); harmless only if the core, its reconstruction LPF (450 Hz) and the Time readout are explicitly designed for it.
